narrative.intro: Fluor Marine Propulsion shows $4.3B in federal contract obligations for FY2026 to date. Fluor Marine Propulsion received 2 awards so far this fiscal year, with an average award size of $2.1B and obligations up 19.9% year over year. Fiscal-year obligations have risen from $3.1B in FY21 to $4.3B in FY26, with intermediate levels of $3.6B in FY22, $3.5B in FY23, $3.5B in FY24, and $3.6B in FY25. The Department of Defense is the largest buyer, obligating $2.3B, followed by the Department of Energy at $1.9B. All figures are contract obligations except award-value figures noted elsewhere, and current-year totals are partial (fiscal year to date). This profile reflects a concentrated set of high-value awards and a small number of buyers driving most obligations. Contractors and partners should note the concentration of obligations by agency and the small award count when assessing competitive and teaming opportunities with Fluor Marine Propulsion during the current fiscal year.

sections.heading: How has Fluor Marine Propulsion's federal business trended by year?
sections.body: Fluor Marine Propulsion's obligations rose from $3.1B in FY21 to $3.6B in FY22, then held near $3.5B in FY23 and FY24, and returned to $3.6B in FY25 before reaching $4.3B in FY26 to date. Fluor Marine Propulsion's year-over-year obligations are up 19.9% for the current fiscal year-to-date period.

sections.heading: Who are the biggest federal buyers of Fluor Marine Propulsion?
sections.body: The Department of Defense obligated $2.3B to Fluor Marine Propulsion in FY2026 to date. The Department of Energy obligated $1.9B to Fluor Marine Propulsion in the same period.
